title: The Pure water from the spring
subtitle: 自然生态 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 自然生态（自然生态·自然与荒野）
meta: 主题语境：自然生态（自然生态·自然与荒野）　|　核心词汇：pure　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 pure 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1990 the guide wrote of ① a pure water from the spring in the guidebook, and everybody in the valley said at once that it was ② so pure that nobody in the valley would go near it. Three days on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the guide, who never explained anything, had done it in silence and gone home; it was the pure ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the pure water from the spring that anybody there had ever seen, or so the guidebook for July 1984 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too pure to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the traveller who had come to help; the pure ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the map at the far ledge, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a pure joy of the child, and said that no traveller in his right mind would call it ⑥ as pure as the joy of the child they had once had in the old valley. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was pure or not, and he said so.

By 1997 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the guidebook. What the line asked for was ⑦ something pure, and nothing besides. The traveller from the next valley called the whole plan ⑧ quite pure; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the guidebook kept the names of the pure ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 2000, twice over, she wrote of another pure water from the spring in the same guidebook, and the work, which took two days, seemed ⑨ no less pure than anybody had expected. ⑩ The pure joy of the child that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 2002, was the one she could never quite name; the pure ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 纯净（前置定语 a pure water from the spring：1990 年向导在旅行手册里记下的那件纯净的水）
B. adj. 纯净／纯真（两处加强说法：so pure that … 与 no less pure than …）
C. adj. 纯净／纯真（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 纯净（表语 too pure to do：母亲觉得它太纯净，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 纯真（前置定语 a pure joy of the child：叔叔把整件事称作一桩纯真的快乐）
F. adj. 纯真（同级比较 as pure as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩孩子纯真的快乐相比）
G. adj. 纯真（后置定语 something pure：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 纯真（受程度副词修饰 quite pure：那位旅人的评价）

items.q: a pure water from the spring
the pure water from the spring that
a pure joy of the child
The pure joy of the child that

answers.why: pure 意为“纯净”，1990 年向导在旅行手册里记下的是“一件纯净的水”，此处作前置定语 a pure water from the spring。
pure 意为“纯净”，此处用 so pure that 结构，说它纯净到山谷里没人敢靠近。
pure 意为“纯净”，旅行手册上 七月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的纯净泉眼里纯净的水，等于最高级的说法。
pure 意为“纯净”，母亲认为这件东西“太纯净了，谁也用不上”，too pure to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
pure 意为“纯真”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩纯真的快乐”，此处作前置定语 a pure joy of the child。
pure 意为“纯真”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩孩子纯真的快乐一样纯真”，同级比较用 as pure as。
pure 意为“纯真”，旅行手册上那半行字要的是“纯真的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something pure。
pure 意为“纯真”，邻山谷来的那位旅人认为这套计划“相当纯真”，quite 修饰原级 pure。
pure 意为“纯真”，no less pure than 表示“其纯真不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之纯真不亚于任何人的预料。
pure 意为“纯真”，母亲 2002 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的纯真快乐”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1990 年，向导在旅行手册里记下了一件纯净的水。（a pure water from the spring）
它纯净到山谷里没有一个人敢靠近。（so pure that …）
母亲觉得它太纯净，谁也用不上。（too pure to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩纯真的快乐。（a pure joy of the child）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩孩子纯真的快乐一样纯真。（as pure as …）
到了 1997 年，旅行手册上只剩半行字：要的是一件纯真的东西。（something pure）
answers: In 1990 the guide wrote of a pure water from the spring in the guidebook.
It was so pure that nobody in the valley would go near it.
My mother thought it too pure to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a pure joy of the child.
He said nobody would call it as pure as the joy of the child they had once had.
By 1997 the guidebook asked for nothing but something pure.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 pure 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1990 the guide wrote of a pure water from the spring in the guidebook, and nobody forgot it.
It was the pure water from the spring that anybody there had ever seen, or so the guidebook says.
My mother thought it too pure to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a pure joy of the child, and nobody argued with him.
The traveller from the next valley called the plan quite pure, and everybody laughed.
The pure ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
